To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we derived the capture-zone distribution function for generic aggregation-limiting conditions, (2) we found a general equality between α and β, and (3) we measured the critical nucleus size of pentacene on mica.
the scaling and exponent equalities are generally valid for compact island nucleation, and that they can be applied to measure critical nucleus sizes in organic films, and possibly other systems.
the scaling exponent α and the exponent β in the capture-zone distribution function are related by the equality αβ = i, the critical nucleus size, in the case when the aggregation is compact.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the growth and morphology of thin films.
the scaling of island densities in thin-film growth and the application of this scaling to the determination of the critical nucleus sizes for the growth of organic semiconducting materials.
scaling and exponent equalities in the nucleation of clusters in thin films.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the exponent equalities are not universal but are valid in a limited range of deposition parameters and are valid only if the critical nucleus size is constant.
the scaling and exponent equalities, as well as the capture-zone distribution function, apply to all systems with a critical nucleus size i, irrespective of the actual aggregation-limiting process.

the critical nucleus size in the case of diffusion limited aggregation is given by the expression i = α/β = 4·D·t0/π·h2, where D is the diffusion coefficient, t0 the time of the first nucleation event, and h the height of the critical nucleus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for compact islands, the exponent β of P(s) = aβ·sβ·e-bβs2 is related to the exponent α and to the critical nucleus i by the equality i/α = β.
the exponent α is a direct probe of the critical nucleus i and of the aggregation limiting mechanism.
the exponent equalities are a general feature of island nucleation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the critical nucleus size can be measured from the scaling of the island density with the deposition rate, without any a priori information on the aggregation mechanism.
the scaling and exponent equalities are not limited to diffusion-limited aggregation, as previously assumed.
the scaling of N with F is not a universal property of thin-film deposition.
